justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: TBI rehabilitation evidence supports specialized, coordinated care; CBIS-specific outcomes not studied.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Online modules plus CBIS exam; moderate cost and time; accessible pathway.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable in TBI and acquired brain injury programs; moderate applicability in neuro and acute care settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: TBI rehab billed under standard PT/OT/SLP codes; CBIS supports brain injury program authorization and quality documentation in some health systems.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate demand in TBI programs, inpatient rehab, and brain injury specialty clinics.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: TBI patients and families value clinicians who understand the unique challenges of brain injury.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: TBI rehab is overwhelmingly insurance/Medicaid/waiver funded; families rarely pay cash for brain injury services and case management is the dominant payer pathway.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: CBIS is recognized in post-acute and neuro settings but doesn't command premium DTC pricing — it's an employer-required credential, not a consumer brand.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Moderately uncommon among outpatient PTs but standard in neuro post-acute facilities, so differentiation depends heavily on local market.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Possible to build a concussion/TBI niche clinic around it, but most revenue still flows through insurance contracts limiting cash-pay scale.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Consumers don't search for 'CBIS' — they search for concussion clinics or neuro rehab; weak brand recognition.
justifications.business.efficiency: Relatively cheap (~$400) exam-based credential with no residency requirement, so ROI per dollar is reasonable.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Held by some neuro faculty but not weighted heavily for tenure or hiring versus NCS or a residency; nice-to-have, not differentiating.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Modest TBI literature among CBIS holders; the credential itself isn't a scholarship engine but aligns with a publishable clinical area.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Useful content for neuro and acute care DPT/MOT courses, especially TBI/concussion modules.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: TBI rehab has a growing but heterogeneous evidence base — RCTs exist for specific interventions, less for general rehab pathways.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed as required or preferred in PT/OT faculty job ads; NCS is the dominant neuro credential sought.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Low time/cost burden relative to a neuro residency, making it an efficient way to signal TBI competence.
